terms.gloss: ambition, desire for honours; at Rome, canvassing for office
evidence: Cic. Sull. 11: mea mē ambitiō ab omnī illā cōgitātiōne abstrahēbat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “going round” the voters; lawful canvassing, where ambitus is bribery.

sources: Lewis & Short: ambitio · Lewis & Short: ambitiosus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 271.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
